idea-plugin.name: Taskbar Ungroup
idea-plugin.description:
Taskbar Ungroup gives every IntelliJ IDEA project window its own button on the Windows taskbar.

IntelliJ IDEA is a single-process, multi-window application: all project windows share one process-level AppUserModelID, so Windows groups them into a single taskbar button. This plugin assigns each project window a unique window-level AppUserModelID (PKEY_AppUserModel_ID) right after the project opens, which makes the taskbar show one button per project — no external helper process required.

  • Applies automatically within milliseconds of a project window opening (no IDE restart needed).
  • Stable AppUserModelID derived from the project path hash — the same project always gets the same identity.
  • Windows only; silently inactive on Linux/macOS.

中文说明：让每个 IntelliJ 项目窗口在 Windows 任务栏上显示为独立按钮（取消合并），同一项目标识稳定不变。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.1: all windows of the same project now share the project's identity — previously only the first window of a project was ungrouped, so a second window (Open in New Window, torn-off editor tab) fell back into the default IDE group. The post-startup fallback no longer gives up when JNA is not yet loaded (the service retries and self-heals). Window lookup now uses the frame handle directly, removing the by-title matching that could mis-apply when two projects had identical window titles.

0.2.0: first project window after IDE startup now applies the AUMID at window show time — the platform shows the frame before the project is attached to it, so the plugin polls for project attachment (150 ms) instead of waiting for startup completion.

Initial release (0.1.0): per-project window AppUserModelID with auto-apply, retry on not-yet-ready windows, and silent no-op on non-Windows systems.
